title: trigger.is_terminal now marks unrecognized status strings terminal via the Failed fallback, freeing slots
evidence:
fn is_terminal(status: String) -> Bool {
-  list.contains(
-    [
-      "form_completed",
-      "unreachable",
-      "refused",
-      "objected",
-      "manual_recorded",
-      "failed",
-      "completed",
-      "partial",
-    ],
-    status,
-  )
+  is_terminal_status(status_from_string(status))
 }

+/// terminal-looking outcome on the wire). Status's own fallback is inert by
+/// design: an unrecognised status decodes to `Failed`, so hooks and the rendered
+/// status can never diverge on the wire.
detail: Old list returned False for any unrecognized string (slot stays occupied). New chain: status_from_string falls back to Failed (per the diff's own docs), and is_terminal_status(Failed) is True — so corrupt or expand-window statuses now free their slot.
recommended_fix: Keep unknown statuses non-terminal in is_terminal: decode via status_from_string but treat only the known terminal set as terminal, or document the slot-freed behavior explicitly.

title: Spec says the em-dash lint excludes copy.gleam; the shipped script scans it wholesale
evidence:
- Lint: `scripts/lint_em_dash.py` — fails on em-dash inside string literals
  in user-facing source (client/src except copy.gleam — the spec-verbatim
  home — plus the server form/refcheck view surface). Wired as a CI step in
  `test.yml` (unit-test job, alongside the existing grep lints).

Scope: user-facing render/composition modules (client/src wholesale,
including copy.gleam, plus the server form/refcheck surface and the detail
handler).
detail: The spec (same PR) declares copy.gleam the blanket exempt home, but the implemented lint scans it with per-owner exemptions and also adds application_detail_handler.gleam beyond the spec'd surface. Spec-verbatim copy not yet listed in SPEC_VERBATIM_OWNERS would fail CI contrary to the spec.
recommended_fix: Update the spec's item 4 scope text to match the implemented owner-exemption approach (including the detail handler), or restore the wholesale copy.gleam exclusion.

title: Lockstep test direction 2 hardcodes the 14 status strings the guard exists to prevent mirroring
detail: The test's own doc condemns hardcoded mirror copies (#610 r1 B1), yet direction 2 reintroduces one: a 15th terminal status missing from this hand-maintained list is silently unverified, so the reverse-direction lockstep does not actually lock.
recommended_fix: Derive direction 2 from the shared package (e.g. an exported status-string list) or generate the list so it cannot drift from the enum.

title: lint_refcheck_hooks.py checks for a ':' token its own TOKEN_RE never produces
detail: TOKEN_RE emits no colon, so the ':' member of the pending_case reset tuple is dead. If the intent was to reset on ':' (e.g. type annotations in case subjects), it silently never fires.
recommended_fix: Either remove ":" from the tuple or add a colon alternative to TOKEN_RE so the reset actually applies.
